userDrawer.boundNoteStrict: Each device has keys of its own, and the device limit is the number of places. Apps without a device ID get no subscription. An unbound device is cut off at once.
userDrawer.unbindText: The device loses access at once and its place frees up. If it is connected with the link again, it takes a place again.
userDrawer.unbindSharedText: Apps without a device ID lose access at once: their shared keys change. The subscription link stays, they reconnect after refreshing the subscription.
userDrawer.needOneProtocol: At least one protocol is needed, otherwise disable the client
userDrawer.telegramNone: Not in the bot. The subscriber can connect it from the subscription page.
userDrawer.telegramUnlinkText: The bot stops showing it to that account and sending notices.
userDrawer.notePlaceholder: E.g.: pays via Telegram, renew on the 1st

torrent.title: Torrents
torrent.exemptHint: The torrent blocker leaves this client alone.

tariffs.subtitle: Templates for granting access in one click. Changing a plan does not touch subscriptions already issued.
tariffs.emptyText: Create a template, e.g. «Standard: 150 GB for 30 days, 3 devices».
tariffs.archiveText: New clients cannot be created with it. Nothing changes for those who already have it.
tariffs.name: Name
tariffs.termToDate: To a day of the month
tariffs.monthsHint: In months; 0 means never expires. A month runs to the same day of the next month, not 30 days.
tariffs.billingDayHint: Terms always end on this day. The first one ends on the nearest such day at least 15 days away. A month without this day ends on its last day.
tariffs.whenResetHint: For multi-month plans: the volume is granted again every period.
tariffs.saleSub: The plan shows in the bot and the Mini App: once paid, the panel issues or renews the subscription itself.
tariffs.priceRubHint: For YooKassa and CryptoBot (it converts to the coin picked).
tariffs.moreTermsSub: The same plan for another term and price: in the bot and the Mini App the buyer picks the term. Traffic resets by the plan's rule.

presets.vless_reality_xhttp: Main one for Russia: looks like plain HTTPS and keeps few connections
presets.hysteria2: Fast on poor links, runs over UDP
presets.hysteria2_gecko: Hysteria2 against QUIC blocking by packet size. Only on mihomo 1.19.26+, other apps get plain Hysteria2
presets.tuic_v5: A QUIC alternative, also over UDP
presets.vless_reality_vision: For old clients without XHTTP. Gets frozen quickly on 443 in Russia
presets.vless_reality_grpc: HTTP/2 with multiplexing: few connections, a different traffic pattern
presets.trojan_reality: Another protocol under the same camouflage, a fallback
presets.vless_tls_xhttp: Plain TLS on the real certificate of the panel's domain, like a website: answers strangers as a web server, keeps few connections
presets.vless_tls_vision: Classic VLESS Vision on the real certificate of the panel's domain: works in almost every app. Gets frozen quickly on 443 in Russia
presets.anytls: TLS with padding against packet-size analysis. Needs a mihomo or sing-box app
presets.vless_reality_xhttp_pq: XHTTP with post-quantum encryption: traffic recorded today stays sealed in the future too. Needs a recent mihomo or Xray, sing-box will not connect
presets.trusttunnel: AdGuard's protocol: HTTP/2 on the node's real certificate, looks like a regular website
presets.shadowquic: QUIC that answers strangers like a real website (JLS). A spare UDP protocol
presets.mieru: Its own encryption and a random traffic pattern. TCP only
presets.shadowsocks_2022: The classic: fast and understood by every app. One key for all clients
presets.sudoku: Hides traffic as HTTP and text. One key for all clients
presets.snell: The Surge app's protocol. One key for all clients
presets.custom: Your own mihomo protocol settings in the editor: any supported type and parameters

inbounds.subtitle: Protocols clients use to reach the server. Keys and passwords are generated automatically.
inbounds.reconnectWarning: After changing the port or camouflage, clients reconnect on their own within a few seconds. Hysteria2 and TUIC take longer, up to 30 seconds.
inbounds.emptyText: Without them clients cannot connect. Start with VLESS REALITY XHTTP, it works best in Russia.
inbounds.deleteText: Clients using this protocol lose the connection until they switch to another one. Subscriptions update by themselves.
inbounds.errPortBusy: The port is used by another program on the server. Choose another port or free this one.
inbounds.errPermission: No permission to open this port. Check the container settings.
inbounds.newMeta: Keys, passwords and paths are generated automatically
inbounds.portHint: Default {port}/{network}. Hysteria2 accepts a range, e.g. 20000-20100.
inbounds.saved: Saved. Clients get the changes when their subscription updates
inbounds.subNameHint: Clients see the protocol under this name. Emoji are fine: «🇳🇱 Netherlands». Empty: the default name.
inbounds.destHint: A site with TLS 1.3 and HTTP/2, ideally in the server's network. From outside, the connection looks like a visit to this site.
inbounds.destLocked: The settings were changed on the «Settings (YAML)» tab, change the site there too.
inbounds.destHintIP: The IP of a site next to the server: the node relays other people's probes of the port there. Outsiders see the domain below, not the IP.
inbounds.sniHint: From outside, the connection looks like a visit to this site. If an IP is set above, its certificate must match this site.
inbounds.sniRequired: Enter the site: clients cannot connect without it
inbounds.fingerprintHint: If the connection starts getting blocked, try another browser.
inbounds.fingerprintLocked: The settings were changed on the «Settings (YAML)» tab, change the browser there too (mikan.client.fingerprint).
inbounds.customMeta: mihomo protocol settings: mikan adds clients, port and certificate itself
inbounds.configHint: For advanced users. The panel adds the port, the client list and the certificate itself. Ctrl+Space shows hints.
inbounds.portHintCustom: A free port: TCP or UDP depends on the type in the config.
inbounds.customSkeleton:
# mihomo protocol settings. mikan fills in name, port, listen,
# users and the certificate. Types: vless, vmess, trojan, hysteria2, tuic, anytls.
type: trojan
ws-path: /ws
mikan:
  tls: node   # the node certificate, like Hysteria2 and TUIC
inbounds.targetScanning: Looking for sites in the server's network, up to 30 seconds…
inbounds.targetNone: No suitable sites near the server (addresses checked: {scanned}). Keep a popular site or set the server's domain in the settings.
inbounds.targetSelfStealHint: Own domain: the camouflage site matches the server, with the panel's Let's Encrypt certificate

targetErr.timeout: The site did not answer in time
targetErr.dns: The site address was not found
targetErr.private: The name leads to an internal address: only public sites are checked
targetErr.sni_required: An IP needs the site's domain (SNI)
targetErr.cert: The certificate does not match the name

inbounds.nodeEmptyText: Add protocols: they appear in the subscription with the node's flag.
inbounds.autoPort: Move to another port when it is blocked
inbounds.autoPortSub: If your provider starts blocking the port, the panel moves the connection to another one by itself. Same if another program takes the port.
inbounds.autoSni: Replace the camouflage site when it stops working
inbounds.autoSniSub: The server checks the site every 15 minutes. After three failures in a row it picks another working site nearby, never its own domain.
inbounds.autoOffGlobal: Off in settings, not active now
inbounds.proxySub: Only needed if port 443 is already taken by nginx or HAProxy. Otherwise change nothing.
inbounds.listen: Which address the protocol works on
inbounds.listenAllHint: The protocol is open to the outside on the port above.
inbounds.listenLocalHint: Not reachable from outside: a proxy on this server forwards to {addr}.
inbounds.listenCustomHint: One IP address of this server, e.g. an internal address for a proxy on another machine.
inbounds.clientHint: Empty: as now, the node's address and the protocol's port. The node accepts connections on its own port.
inbounds.clientHintReality: Empty: as now, the node's address and the protocol's port. With REALITY the SNI is the camouflage site, which is how the proxy tells the protocol apart.
inbounds.clientPortWarn: Clients will go to port {port}, which is closed to the outside. Enter the proxy's port, usually 443.
inbounds.clientLocked: The settings were changed on the «Settings (YAML)» tab, change the client address there (mikan.client).
inbounds.autoPortProxy: Behind a proxy the port does not move: the proxy would not know the new one.
inbounds.autoSniProxy: Behind a proxy the site does not change: the proxy may route by the site's name and would lose the clients.

xhttp.intro: How XHTTP requests look on the wire. Server settings go to the apps with the subscription. An empty field is the core's default.
xhttp.strongWarn: Only recent apps: Happ and v2RayTun on a new Xray, Clash apps on mihomo 1.19.31+. Older versions cannot connect to this protocol.
xhttp.modeHint: By default the core picks one. packet-up gets through almost everywhere, stream-one is faster.
xhttp.rangeHint: A number or a range like 500-3000: each request gets a random size.
xhttp.obfsHint: The padding goes to a place of your choice under its own name instead of Referer: such requests are harder to recognise.
xhttp.reuseHint: How many streams an app sends through one HTTP/2 connection and how long it keeps it. Fewer new connections mean fewer noticeable TLS handshakes.
xhttp.connectionsHint: Instead of streams per connection, not with them.

inbounds.cutOffOf: Devices that cannot reach it: {n} of {total}

stuck.off: Automatic fixes are off for this protocol.
stuck.waiting: The port or site was just changed. Waiting for clients to update their subscription.
stuck.no_port: Every port autotune moves a protocol to is taken (2053, 2083, 2087, 2096, 2443–9443 in steps of 1000, 10443–12443). Turn off a protocol you do not need or move one to another port.
stuck.no_target: No other suitable site next to the server.
stuck.exhausted: Changing the port and the site did not help: the protocol itself is probably blocked. Try another one.

inbounds.targetDown: The camouflage site does not respond: {reason}

reason.still_blocked: a new port did not help
reason.busy: another program on the server held the port

inbounds.clashOnlyNote: Only Clash apps on a recent mihomo get it: Koala Clash, SlothClash, FlClash, Clash Verge, ClashFest. Happ, v2RayTun and Hiddify will not see it.
inbounds.domainCertNote: The certificate is a real one on the panel's node when the panel has a domain, and on a node with a certificate of its own. Other nodes use a self-signed one: apps check it against the pin in the subscription, but from outside the port no longer looks like an ordinary website.
inbounds.sharedWarn: This protocol has one key for everyone. Traffic counting, limits and devices do not work on it, and a disabled client keeps access until the key changes. To change the key, delete the protocol and add it again.
inbounds.outboundWarpHint: All traffic goes through the node's WARP, sites see a Cloudflare address. If WARP is down the protocol stops working: traffic does not go direct.
inbounds.outboundNoWarp: The node has no WARP or it is off, so traffic goes direct for now. Set WARP up on the Nodes page.
inbounds.outboundNodeHint: Clients connect to this node and leave to the internet through the chosen one: sites see its address. If that node is down, traffic does not go direct.
inbounds.obfsHint: Every app with Hysteria2 knows Salamander. Gecko also hides QUIC from blocking by packet size.
inbounds.obfsGeckoHint: Gecko works on mihomo 1.19.26+ (Koala Clash 1.4+, ClashFest 1.2+, SlothClash 0.9.4+). Other apps will not get it, so keep a plain Hysteria2 next to it.
inbounds.portHopHint: A range such as 20000-30000 works too: clients switch ports on the go, so one port cannot be blocked. Open the range over UDP in the server firewall.

settings.subtitle: Server address, subscription look and sign-in security
settings.themeSub: The panel color scheme is saved in this browser.
settings.hostHint: The IP address clients use to connect to the VPN.
settings.domainHint: Optional. When set, links use it instead of the IP.
settings.quietHourHint: Once a day at this hour some clients briefly reconnect. Pick the time when the fewest people are online.
settings.subscriptionSub: How the profile looks in clients' apps
settings.brandHint: The profile gets this name in clients' apps.
settings.groupMainHint: This is the list name in Clash apps. Usually «VPN».
settings.groupAutoHint: The item that picks the fastest server by itself.
settings.previewHint: This is how the subscription looks in Clash apps. Server names are changed under «Protocols».
settings.routingHint: For every app: Clash apps get all of it, sing-box (SFA, SFI, SFM) nearly all, Happ and INCY the sites and IPs when Subscription → Happ says so.
settings.routingRuDirectSub: Russian sites and IPs bypass the VPN by mihomo geodata: banks and state services work, and the server does not carry that traffic.
settings.routingAllSub: All traffic except the local network goes through the server.
settings.routingBlockedSub: Sites and apps blocked or slowed down in Russia (the privWL-clash lists) and the services sent to the VPN below go through it. The rest goes direct.
settings.routesSub: What goes through the VPN, what goes direct and what is blocked. For Koala Clash, FlClash, Clash Verge and other apps on mihomo.
settings.routesServicesHint: "Like the rest" follows the mode above. "Server" always sends the service through that node; the app shows it as a group of its own.
settings.routesAppsHint: Apps and sites that need a local address. On Android and computers the rules go by the app's name, on iPhones by the sites.
settings.routesDnsHint: Empty: the panel's DNS. A server is written as in mihomo: an IP or an address like https://…, tls://…, quic://…; with #PROXY at the end the query goes through the VPN.
settings.routesDnsProxyHint: How the app finds the VPN servers themselves, one per line (proxy-server-nameserver).
settings.routesDnsPolicy: DNS of your own for domains
settings.routesDnsPolicyHint: A line per "domains: servers separated by commas", e.g. +.cn: https://dns.alidns.com/dns-query (nameserver-policy).
settings.routesNote: Clash apps (Koala Clash, FlClash, Clash Verge, ClashFest) get all of it. The official sing-box apps (SFA, SFI, SFM) a config with the groups, services and DNS, without XHTTP and servers with a self-signed certificate. Happ and INCY the sites and IPs when Subscription → Happ is set to From the routing settings. v2RayTun, v2rayNG, Hiddify and Karing get links only: they route by their own settings.
settings.routesPreviewSub: The Clash profile of a client with every protocol and these settings, before they are saved. Its keys are placeholders.
settings.routesYamlOn: Clash apps get the own YAML
settings.routesListsHint: Any rule list by link (a mihomo rule-provider): your whitelist, privWL, community lists. Apps download it through the VPN and update it daily. Happ takes from it only what its geodata has.
settings.routesServersSub: How the groups of servers look in the apps.
settings.routesAutoFastestHint: The app tests every server and keeps the fastest.
settings.routesAutoFallbackHint: The app keeps the first working server in the nodes' order and moves on only when it fails. Fewer switches.
settings.routesIntervalHint: How often the app tests servers for the auto choice and the country groups.
settings.routesCountriesSub: With several nodes each gets a group of its own, the fastest server inside.
settings.routesQuicSub: No UDP to port 443: browsers and YouTube fall back to TCP, which gets through the tunnel better where QUIC is throttled.
settings.routesSniffer: Read the site from the connection (sniffer)
settings.routesSnifferSub: Rules by domain work for apps that connect by IP too.
settings.routesRealIPSub: For apps that break on fake addresses; every connection waits for DNS.
settings.routesYamlLive: Clash apps get your own YAML now (the Own YAML view): the settings below do not reach them. Stash and apps not on mihomo get the simple profile.
settings.templateSub: A whole mihomo config: DNS, fake-ip, TUN, sniffer, your groups and rules. The panel adds the client's servers itself.
settings.templateNotLive: Apps get the simple profile for now. Save the YAML and it takes its place in Koala Clash, FlClash, Clash Verge and other apps on mihomo.
settings.templateHowServers: Leave proxies out, the panel adds the client's servers itself. A group gets them through include-all-proxies (with filter, as in mihomo) or through mikan: nodes (those nodes) and types (protocols). If nothing fits, the group gets REJECT.
settings.templateHowNodes: Nodes for mikan: nodes, by name or number:
settings.templateHowRest: The panel puts direct routes to its own servers ahead of your rules. Saving checks for broken YAML, groups without names, and groups and lists that are referred to but do not exist.
settings.templateOffSure: Sure? Apps get the simple profile
settings.fingerprintHint: How clients' apps look to the provider. A protocol can set its own.
settings.autoSub: The panel fixes protocols that stopped working on its own
settings.autoPort: Move to another port when it is blocked
settings.autoPortSub: If your provider starts blocking the port, the panel moves the connection to another one by itself. Same if another program takes the port.
settings.autoSni: Replace the camouflage site when it stops working
settings.autoSniSub: Every 15 minutes the node checks the REALITY camouflage site. After three failures in a row the panel picks a working site next to the server, never its own domain.
settings.autoNote: Clients get the changes with their next subscription update, usually within an hour. Automatic fixes can be turned off for a single protocol in its settings.
settings.updatesSub: The panel checks for new versions once a day
settings.updatesWaitingText: The server pulls the new version and restarts the panel, this page reconnects by itself. VPN pauses for a few seconds.
settings.updatesStale: The server has not taken the request in two minutes. Update on the server with mikan update: the old installer cannot update from the button.
settings.updatesAutoSub: Once a day at night. A backup first, and the current version comes back if the new one does not start.
settings.updatesConfirmText: The server backs up, pulls the signed release and restarts the panel and the node. VPN pauses for a few seconds. If the new version does not start, this one comes back.
settings.updatesHop: This version updates to {v} first, then on to {newest} by itself.
settings.updatesUnreachable: {v} is out, but this version cannot update to it directly.
settings.updatesBetaSub: New versions before everyone else. They can have bugs.
settings.updatesGoalsSub: Show here which features money is being collected for.
settings.updatesNodesSub: One at a time, after the panel. If one fails to update, you get an alert.
settings.langSub: For visitors who have not picked a language yet
settings.langNote: The panel and the subscription page open in this language until a person picks their own. It also sets default names in apps and the bot.
settings.bindingSub: Each device takes a place in the limit. When places run out, a new device sees a message instead of servers.
settings.requireHwid: Only allow apps that identify the device
settings.requireHwidSub: Happ, Koala Clash, v2RayTun and a few more. Other apps will not open the subscription.
settings.devicesNote: A client may unbind one device a day on the subscription page; you can do it any time. A device gets its keys on the next subscription refresh.
settings.supportHint: A Telegram or website link for the «Contact support» button on the subscription page.
settings.appsSub: What subscribers see in their VPN apps besides the servers
settings.announceHint: A line in Happ and v2RayTun: news, maintenance, or the term and traffic left with the variables below. Empty: nothing is shown.
settings.announceUrlHint: Where a tap on the announcement leads: https:// or tg://
settings.appBrandingSub: ClashFest (Android) and SlothClash (Windows, macOS, Linux) show your name, logo and colour, plus links to support, the bot and renewal.
settings.happSub: Happ only: an encrypted link instead of the subscription address, a routing profile and hidden server settings.

happCryptHint.off: The Happ button on the subscription page opens the plain link: its address is visible.
happCryptHint.api: Happ's service encrypts the link: the subscription address goes to crypto.happ.su once. If the service is down, the panel encrypts it itself.
happCryptHint.local: The panel encrypts it and the address goes nowhere. Happ does not publish the format: if it changes, switch to "By Happ".

happRoutingModeHint.off: Happ and INCY route as the person set them up.
happRoutingModeHint.auto: For Happ and INCY. The profile is built from Settings → Routing. A service on a separate server simply goes through the VPN in Happ, which has no rules by app.
happRoutingModeHint.link: A profile made in Happ, unchanged.

settings.happRoutingHint: Build a profile in Happ (Routing → Share) and paste the link. An onadd link turns it on right away, add only adds it. Happ applies it after reconnecting.
settings.happProviderHint: Get it at happ-proxy.com (top right of the profile). Without it Happ will not accept hidden settings.
settings.happHideSub: Clients will not see or change server addresses, keys and parameters in Happ.
settings.happHideNeedsProvider: Save the provider ID first: without it Happ does not hide the settings.
settings.happLinkHint: Encrypted: Happ opens the subscription without showing its address. Reissuing the link makes it invalid.
settings.brandAccentHint: #RRGGBB. Empty: the app's own colour. A colour too pale for both themes is ignored by the app.
settings.brandLogoHint: An https link to a PNG, WebP or JPEG up to 512 KB, square, 256×256. Empty: the app's icon.
settings.adminLinkSub: The panel opens only through this link. Keep it like a password.
settings.newLinkHint: If the link leaked. The old one stops working.
settings.newLinkText: The old link stops working in a few seconds and we switch to the new one right away. Save it: without it you can only sign in through the server (mikan url).
settings.certRequested: Certificate requested, it takes up to a minute
settings.certSelf: Self-signed: browsers warn, and some apps will not accept the subscription
settings.certNote: Renews automatically. Issuance needs port 80 open, it is held for a few seconds.
settings.revokeKeys: Revoke API keys too: a key made from a hijacked session would outlive the password change
settings.newPasswordHint: At least 12 characters. A phrase of several words is handy.
settings.twoFactorOn: On: signing in needs a code from the app
settings.twoFactorOff: A code from an authenticator app at every sign-in
settings.recoveryText: Save the recovery codes: each works once if your phone is not at hand. We will not show them again.
settings.totpQr: QR code for the authenticator app
settings.totpScan: Scan the code in Google Authenticator, 1Password or Aegis and enter the 6 digits.
settings.sessionsSub: Where the panel is open now
settings.fpOwnHint: A uTLS profile name: lowercase letters, digits and _, such as chrome120 or randomizednoalpn. Xray apps may refuse a value off the list, and mihomo connects without uTLS when it does not know it.
settings.fpOwnBad: Lowercase letters, digits and _ only, up to 32 characters
settings.apiSub: Keys for scripts and integrations, and a reference of every panel method.
settings.subPortSub: Subscriptions and the subscription page on a port of their own. 443 or 2053 look like any website, and the admin panel's port stops showing in links.
settings.subPortBusy: Port {port} is taken by another program on the server. Subscriptions go through the panel's port {panel} for now. Pick another port.
settings.subPortHint: Empty: the same as the panel's ({panel}).
settings.subPortInvalid: A port is a number from 1 to 65535
settings.subPortNote: The admin panel will not open on this port, old links keep working. Open a port that is not in the list in the server firewall (ufw allow PORT/tcp).
settings.rulesPlaceholder:
# One rule per line: TYPE,VALUE,TARGET
DOMAIN-SUFFIX,example.com,DIRECT
GEOSITE,youtube,PROXY
settings.rulesHint: One rule per line; lines starting with # are comments. A rule with a mistake is not saved. The rules reach Clash apps and sing-box, Happ and INCY their sites and IPs. v2RayTun and Hiddify get none: they route by their own settings.
settings.rulesTypesText: DOMAIN, DOMAIN-SUFFIX, DOMAIN-KEYWORD, GEOSITE, GEOIP, IP-CIDR, IP-CIDR6, IP-SUFFIX, SRC-IP-CIDR, DST-PORT, SRC-PORT, NETWORK, PROCESS-NAME, PROCESS-PATH work in every mihomo app. DOMAIN-REGEX, IP-ASN, SRC-GEOIP (core 1.18+) and DOMAIN-WILDCARD (1.19.12+) reach only apps that name their core, or an older core would fail the whole profile. no-resolve is for GEOIP, IP-CIDR, IP-CIDR6, IP-SUFFIX and IP-ASN.
settings.certOwnNote: Renewed by your own tools: the panel picks a new file up without a restart.

import.title: Clients from another panel
import.sub: Marzban, PasarGuard or Remnawave: clients come over with their limit, usage, term and device limit. Names mikan already has are left out.
import.urlHint: As you open it in the browser, without the admin path: https://panel.example.com. The old panel keeps working; nothing is changed there.
import.tokenHint: Remnawave → API tokens: a token with read access to clients.
import.apiKeyHint: PasarGuard → API keys, with users:read. Leave empty to sign in with the username and password.
import.noLink: {n} come over without the old link: their token is too short to be a secret
import.onHold: {n} on hold: their term in mikan starts at the import, as mikan has no wait for the first connection
import.tariffHint: Clients get the plan's protocols, reset strategy and pools; the limit, term and devices come from the old panel.
import.started: The import has started; you may leave the page
import.invalid: Cannot be taken as they are (too long, broken numbers): {n}
import.notCarried: Not carried over: the traffic reset strategy, groups and protocols of the old panel (clients get the plan's). An on-hold term starts at the import. Links revoked in the old panel work again: reissue them.
import.skipped: {n} left out: the name is taken
import.legacySub: Point the old panel's domain at this server and set its subscription port in Settings → Subscription: the links people have keep working.
import.legacyPathHint: sub for Marzban and PasarGuard, api/sub for Remnawave (or your own). Empty: off.
import.secret: Signing secret of the old panel
import.secretHint: Marzban and PasarGuard sign every link: without their secret an old link cannot be told from a forged one, so it does not open. The secret is in the old panel's database: SELECT secret_key FROM jwt;
import.secretSet: The secret is set. Type a new one to change it.
import.legacyCount: Old links and clients on file: {n}

torrent.title: Torrent blocker
torrent.sub: Nodes recognise BitTorrent and do not let it through: the handshake, DHT, uTP and trackers.
torrent.enableHint: Every node looks at the first bytes of each connection. Encrypted BitTorrent looks like noise and gets through: the blocker catches most clients, not all.
torrent.banHint: A ban cuts the client's connections and keeps them off every node for that long.
torrent.exemptNone: Nobody. Switch the check off for a client in their card.
torrent.hitsSub: The latest catches. A node reports a client at most once a minute; ×N is how many attempts that stands for.

settings.subTitle: Subscription name in apps
settings.subTitleHint: The profile name (the profile-title header) in the apps that read it: Happ, v2RayTun, Hiddify. Clash apps may name the profile after the file instead. Empty: the brand.
settings.unknownVars: Not a variable, it stays as text: {vars}

titleVar.name: The client's name
titleVar.date: When the term ends, DD.MM.YYYY (Moscow time); ∞ without one
titleVar.total: The traffic limit with packages; ∞ without one

page.leaveText: Your changes to the subscription page aren't saved yet and will be lost.
page.resetText: Look, blocks, apps, link preview and custom CSS go back to the defaults. The change applies once you save.
page.themeSub: The panel's palettes, light or dark. Subscribers see the theme on the page and in the Mini App.
page.modeSystemHint: The page is light or dark, whatever the subscriber's device uses.
page.brandAccentHint: Apps with branding get the same colour.
page.bgImageHint: PNG, JPEG or WebP up to 2 MB. Uploaded right away, subscribers see it once you save.
page.bgDimHint: The busier the image, the more it needs dimming to keep text readable.
page.typeSub: Fonts ship with the panel: nothing is loaded from other sites.

fonts.default: Unbounded and Onest, like the panel

page.cardsGlassHint: Translucent, the background shows through a little.
page.cardsSolidHint: Opaque: text reads well over any background.
page.brandSub: The page header and the browser tab.
page.brandNameHint: Apps and the Telegram bot show the same name.
page.subtitle: Line under the name
page.subtitleHint: For example, "Fast VPN for friends". Empty: no line.
page.logoHint: Shown in the page header and on the browser tab.
